items.text: Ha dì, mes cor sa fraisa.
items.q: Maman quotes a lonely friend who has nothing to do all day. A Persian saying kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Mentaunta ri, Hooman ma dà ina paletgada fort sin la schina ed il toc da zucher ma sauta en la gula.
items.q: Hooman thumps Amir on the back while he drinks tea. A Persian image kept word for word: is it clear what happens?

items.text: Bibi, che Dieu al perdunia, diseva en talas occasiuns: sche di, brischa mia lingua; sche na di betg, brischa la maregl da mes ossa.
items.q: Maman hesitates before criticising her husband. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: La plievgia n'croda betg da la terra versa il tschiel.
items.q: Her son says he would die for her; Maman objects. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Di: «In bun onn sa recunuscha da sia primavaira.»
items.q: The family's New Year visits were cancelled; a brother jokes about it. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Tge che jau di è che, sche restas qua sesì a leger poesia, na til vegn a s'stgaudar il paun.
items.q: A friend criticises Amir for reading poetry all day. A Persian expression kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Mo suenter che la famiglia m'aveva metì a forza en il pulaliu hai chapì tge mund tant different era quel da l'autra vart da l'istorgia.
items.q: A friend talks about his own life after his family pushed him. A Persian expression kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Mia maun è curta e tia uniun è luntsch.
items.q: Amir tells the girl he loves why he holds back. A Persian expression kept word for word: is the meaning clear?
